claims: The phase-change attempt completed 69/69 retained solver runs and passed numerical finiteness and linear-residual guards.
The attempt is an equivalent surface latent-heat proxy from the existing total-C Robin boundary loss, not an independently solved liquid-vapor-bound-water model.
Total-C water balance is numerically small, but phase-resolved mass-energy closure fails because phase inventories and phase-resolved fluxes are absent.
Q2/Q3/Q4 identifiability has Jacobian rank 1 of 2 and infinite condition number; Lv and proxy_scale are inseparable.
Independent space and time event ladders exceed the preregistered 60 s tolerance.
The internal-temperature completion has Q2/Q3 fixed-domain energy residuals near 1.9 and Q4 residuals near 1.97-1.99, so it does not establish a reliable improved temperature model.
assumptions: All audited candidate directories are treated as prototypes and not as authority to modify the formal route.
A small numerical heat residual for the proxy is not evidence of phase-resolved physical validity.
The direct classification uses the strongest demonstrated gate: formal promotion is blocked; paper use is sensitivity-only.
unknowns: No internal temperature observations are available for validation.
No material-specific enthalpy/DSC, phase-resolved moisture, vapor RH/concentration, or independently measured phase-change kinetics are available in the audited inputs.
The existing files do not prove that the 19:29 raw run was executed by the later 19:33 script version; a frozen-source rerun is required for clean provenance.
